papers.title: Complete Intersection Semigroups and End Curves on Singularities of Splice Type
papers.abstract: We prove that any complete intersection numerical semigroup can be realized as the value semigroup of an end curve in a splice quotient singularity. Therefore, providing a converse to the semigroup-theoretic statement of the End Curve Theorem of Neumann and Wahl for integral homology sphere links. For a certain family of curves embedded on splice quotient singularities with $\mathbb{Z}HS^3$ link, we show the coincidence between the Alexander polynomial of the knot cutted out by the curve and its Poincar\'e series. Hence providing a generalization of the result due to Campillo, Delgado and Gusein-Zade for plane curve singularities. Moreover, for any complete-intersection numerical semigroup, we define a family of knots such that the Alexander polynomial of the knots coincides with the generating series of the semigroup.

papers.title: Compactifying the $G_2'$-Hitchin component via almost-complex curves
papers.abstract: By studying limits of induced metrics of equivariant almost-complex curves in the pseudosphere $\mathbb{S}^{2,4}$, we compactify the $G_{2}'$-Hitchin component.

papers.title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.

papers.title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem
papers.abstract: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology class, then the sum of all correction terms strictly increases along its surgeries with coefficients -1/j relative to the rational longitude, so no nontrivial surgery yields the original oriented manifold. We also show that every purely cosmetic band surgery on a knot with an L-space branched double cover is weakly nugatory, which answers a question of Rogers for these knots.

papers.title: Systole and kissing number of closed hyperbolic surfaces
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that if the genus of a closed hyperbolic surface $S$ is sufficiently large, then\[ \operatorname{sys}(S)\leq\frac{4}{3}\log(\operatorname{area}(S)). \] This proves a conjecture by Schmutz for large genus. The proof is based on quantitative counting estimates for closed geodesics derived from the Selberg trace formula. As a consequence, we also prove that for such surfaces, the kissing number of $S$ satisfies \[ \operatorname{Kiss}(S) \leq C\frac{\operatorname{area}(S)^{\frac{5}{3}}}{\log(\operatorname{area}(S))}, \] where $C>0$ is a constant.

papers.title: Protection Group of Colored Links
papers.abstract: Colored links provide a mathematical framework for studying the topological stability and classification of three-dimensional topological vortex configurations. Earlier classifications in settings of physical interest relied on system-specific invariants. Here, we introduce a universal invariant of colored links, the \textit{protection group}, interpret earlier classification results as computations of this group, and compute it in new examples.

papers.title: Twisting and foam inequalities for the upsilon invariant
papers.abstract: We describe two families of bounds on the Ozsv\'ath-Stipsicz-Szab\'o invariant $\Upsilon_K(t)$, one controlling its behavior under inserting full twists into a knot and one controlling a limited class of foams, or singular cobordisms between knots. By constructing certain explicit foams, we show that these two formal properties of $\Upsilon$ together exactly determine $\Upsilon_K(t)$ for all torus knots. This generalizes previously observed behavior at $t = 0$, Livingston's slice-torus invariants, and at $t=1$, Sato's unoriented analogue. Our foam bounds on $\Upsilon$ make significant use of Alishahi's generalization of $\Upsilon$ to knotted graphs. Along the way we compute Alishahi's invariant for all theta-graphs lying on the Heegaard torus in $S^3$. We also relate the evaluations of $\Upsilon$ for torus theta-graphs to a distinguished family of properly embedded 2-complexes in the 4-ball sharing many properties with Batson's surfaces.

papers.title: Circular decompositions for hyperbolic genus one knots
papers.abstract: We consider hyperbolic genus one knots having two or more non-isotopic, disjoint, genus one Seifert surfaces, with the property that the complementary regiones are handlebody pairs. We determine whether or not these knots have circular width equal to $(3)$. Moreover we give bounds on their circular widths. We also give explicit examples of such knots having three or five non-isotopic genus one Seifert surfaces and compute their circular widths. In particular this shows that many of these knots are non-almost fibered.

papers.title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
papers.abstract: To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected. As an application, we prove that among one-ended right-angled Coxeter groups, splitting over a subgroup of an unbounded product subgroup is a quasi-isometry invariant. We also establish several features shared by maximized hyperbolic spaces and curve graphs, including the existence of dead ends and visibility of boundaries. Moreover, when the boundary is nonempty, it is non-compact if and only if the defining graph contains an induced 4-cycle.

papers.title: Hurwitz equivalence in quandles of order at most four
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a quandle and let $m\geq 2$ be an integer. The $m$-braid group acts on the $m$-fold Cartesian power $X^m$ by the Hurwitz action. For an $m$-tuple $\boldsymbol{x}\in X^m$, we introduce two invariants of the Hurwitz action: the product $\Pi(\boldsymbol{x})$ of its entries in the associated group $\operatorname{As}(X)$ and the orbit multiplicities $\mu_w(\boldsymbol{x})$ $(w\in X)$. We prove that these two invariants completely classify Hurwitz equivalence classes for all quandles of order at most four. We also establish a complete classification of Hurwitz equivalence classes for a class of amalgamated sums of trivial quandles and a reduction theorem for disjoint sums with trivial quandles. Finally, we study the corresponding action of the virtual braid group. For this action, the orbit multiplicities alone give a complete classification for every quandle of order at most four.

papers.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
papers.abstract: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

papers.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
papers.abstract: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture. In particular, the result applies to every nontrivial satellite knot whose pattern can be unknotted in the solid torus by a single rational tangle replacement.

papers.title: Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants and lattice homology
papers.abstract: For a class of almost rational plumbing 4-manifolds equipped with smooth involutions, we give a description of the Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants of their boundaries in terms of lattice homology. Our approach uses the $S^1$-stable equivalence between Seiberg-Witten Floer spectra and lattice spectra constructed by Dai-Sasahira-Stoffregen, and the $\operatorname{O}(2)$-equivariant versions of these spectra developed by Kang-Park-Taniguchi. As applications, we derive a formula for these invariants for every $\operatorname{spin}^c$ structure on the double branched covers of even torus knots $T_{2p,q}$, and determine the smooth nonorientable $4$-genus of an infinite family of torus knots $T_{4,q}$.

papers.title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
papers.abstract: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

papers.title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
papers.abstract: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent. With $L$ the longitude variable, the specialization contains the irreducible quadratic $E=L^2-(M^4-4M^2+1)L+M^4$ for the negative clasp and $M^4E(M^{-1},L)$ for the positive clasp. The corresponding quadratic is coprime to the full classical $A$-polynomial, including $L-1$, over $\mathbb{Q}(M)[L^{\pm1}]$, so the discrepancy persists when each irreducible factor is counted once. The curve $E=0$ comes from the marked Whitehead link exterior with its axis cusp complete. For the displayed monic polynomial, $\pi m(E)$ is the unsigned volume of that two-cusped exterior. We use the actual Jones sequence to select a right divisor of the satellite transfer operator. Rational factor tests show that the quadratic survives in this divisor, and the two marked companion fillings exclude it as a component of the satellite boundary curve.

papers.title: Symmetries of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology
papers.abstract: We study the behavior of Manolescu's construction of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology under symmetries. Specifically, for k<n we construct a localization spectral sequence from the symplectic sl(n) homology of a knot to the direct sum of the symplectic sl(k) and sl(n-k) homologies of the same knot, giving a geometric analog of rank-reducing spectral sequences arising from deformations on the non-symplectic theory. We also prove the existence of a localization spectral sequence relating the symplectic Khovanov--Rozansky homology of a two-periodic link to the symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the quotient link, in analogy to a theorem of Seidel and Smith for symplectic Khovanov homology. The proofs rely on a generalization of the localization theorem of Seidel-Smith and Large for equivariant Lagrangian Floer cohomology with respect to order two actions; in particular, we extend the theory to the case that the fixed set of the action carries a stable normal real polarization.

papers.title: Geography of Klein bottle Luttinger surgery
papers.abstract: We propose and study a modification of Auroux's uniqueness question on Luttinger surgery by replacing Lagrangian tori with Klein bottles. In Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, we introduce two simple graphs whose connected components give bounds and, in several cases, exact counts of Klein bottle Luttinger equivalence classes. In Kodaira dimension zero, we provide examples of numerical invariants supporting infinitely many equivalence classes and prove a homological non-triviality theorem for Lagrangian Klein bottles in all symplectic Calabi--Yau surfaces with positive Euler characteristic. In positive Kodaira dimensions, we construct examples in which Klein bottle Luttinger surgery changes the symplectic Kodaira dimension.

papers.title: Lagrangian slice disks with symplectomorphic exteriors
papers.abstract: By modifying a construction of Abe and Tange, we exhibit arbitrarily large families of Lagrangian slice disks with Weinstein deformation equivalent exteriors. This answers a Lagrangian version of a question of Hitt and Sumners. We raise other open questions related to Lagrangian slice disks and their exteriors.

papers.title: Fock bundles and Hitchin components
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of a Fock bundle, a smooth principal bundle over a surface equipped with a special kind of adjoint-valued 1-form, as a new tool for studying character varieties of surface groups. Although similar to Higgs bundles, the crucial difference is that no complex structure is fixed on the underlying surface. Fock bundles are the gauge-theoretic realization of higher complex structures. We construct a canonical connection to a Fock bundle equipped with compatible symmetric pairing and hermitian structure. The space of flat Fock bundles maps to the character variety of the split real form. Determining the hermitian structure such that this connection is flat gives a non-linear PDE similar to Hitchin's equation. We explicitly construct solutions for Fock bundles in the Fuchsian locus. Ellipticity of the relevant linear operator provides a map from a neighborhood of the Fuchsian locus in the space of higher complex structures modulo higher diffeomorphisms to a neighborhood of the Fuchsian locus in the Hitchin component.

papers.title: Computer-assisted proofs for the fourth algebraic transfer in certain generic degrees
papers.abstract: This paper restructures the author's earlier article in Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures to correct its erroneous invariant-dimension calculations for the fourth Singer algebraic transfer and is written as a replacement for that article. More precisely, we determine the domain and image of the transfer in the degree families $2^{s+t+1}+2^{s+1}-3$ with $t\ne3$ and $2^{s+t}+2^s-2$ with $t\notin\{2,3,4\}$, where $s,t$ are positive integers. Divided-power spikes are basis elements dual to polynomial monomials whose exponents have the form $2^j-1$ for nonnegative integers $j$. Their translates under ${\rm GL}_4(\mathbb F_2)$, the group of invertible $4\times4$ matrices over the field with two elements, generate submodules of the Steenrod kernel, the subspace annihilated by all positive Steenrod squares. We present these submodules as quotients of sums of permutation modules on complete flags, which are chains in $\mathbb F_2^4$ containing one subspace of each dimension $0,1,2,3,4$. Identifying the relation spaces in these presentations gives explicit equivariant comparison isomorphisms. A recursion obtained by separating even and odd exponents in each variable reduces the comparisons to specified identities of finite-dimensional subspaces. These comparisons apply to both complete degree families, including the parameter values omitted from the transfer theorem. Duplication and partial flag embeddings also give theoretical comparisons in specified parameter ranges. As a consequence, Singer's injectivity conjecture holds in rank four in both degree families under the stated parameter restrictions. The cokernel is one-dimensional in homological degree $256$ and zero in every other degree in those ranges.

papers.title: A new conformal gauge on the visual boundary of a hyperbolic group
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic re-gauging of the visual boundary, arising from the logarithmic metric on the sublinear Morse boundary introduced by Garg-Jana-Qing. For every proper geodesic hyperbolic space $X$, we prove that $d_{\mathrm{log}}(\xi,\eta)\asymp (1+(\xi\mid\eta)_o)^{-\theta}$. As a consequence, under the natural identification of boundaries, $d_{\mathrm{log}}$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to the polynomial Floyd boundary metric associated with the radial density $g_\theta(t)=(1+t)^{-1-\theta}$. Every quasi-isometry between proper geodesic hyperbolic spaces induces a bi-Lipschitz map between their logarithmic boundaries with a fixed admissible exponent. For every non-elementary hyperbolic group, the logarithmic boundary is nondoubling and has infinite Hausdorff and Assouad dimensions. Nevertheless, the logarithmic re-gauging preserves Nagata (capacity) dimension and continues to recover the asymptotic dimension of the group. It also detects one-endedness through linear connectedness (bounded turning) and preserves uniform perfectness. Thus the logarithmic and visual metrics are not quasisymmetrically equivalent, although several coarse-geometric features remain visible in the logarithmic boundary.

papers.title: On Alternateness of the Jones-Kauffman Polynomial of Virtual Links
papers.abstract: We study alternateness of the Jones-Kauffman polynomial of virtual links. In particular, we identify a set of virtual links with alternating Jones-Kauffman polynomial that will be called the set of mock-alternating virtual links. Then, we explain how every mock-alternating virtual link can give rise to an infinite family of mock-alternating virtual links using the twisting technique introduced in [5] and later generalized in [6,20]. Finally, we give a connected state expansion of the mock-determinant for checkerboard-colorable links.

papers.title: A faithful representation and profinite completion
papers.abstract: We exhibit two finitely generated residually finite groups $G_1$ and $G_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{G_1} \cong \widehat{G_2}$, such that $G_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,\mathbb{C})$ but $G_2$ is not linear. This answers a question of Andrei Jaikin-Zapirain, Alexander Lubotzky, and Martin Bridson negatively. Moreover, $G_1$ and $G_2$ form a Grothendieck pair such that every faithful finite-dimensional complex representation of $G_1$ extends uniquely to a nonfaithful representation of $G_2$. We also present two finitely generated residually finite groups $H_1$ and $H_2$ with isomorphic profinite completions $\widehat{H_1} \cong \widehat{H_2}$ satisfying the following. For every field $k$ with characteristic $p \geq 5$ and transcendence degree $r \geq 2$, there exists $d>0$ such that $H_1$ has a faithful representation into $GL(d,k)$. However, $H_2$ admits no faithful finite-dimensional representation over any field of positive characteristic.
